answer: A forged cluster costs real tokens per node, so cheap duplicates lose money. Sybil resistance comes from staking at the wharf: each agent locks a bond before voting, and identities that wander between epochs must re-post collateral. Reputation accrues like a crystal lattice, each honest attestation hardening the structure, while attackers pay twice—once to enter, once when slashed. Because bonds are forfeited on proven duplication, the marginal cost of a fake identity always exceeds its expected reward, making mass identity creation economically irrational.
